app_purpose: Java server-side template engine widely used in Spring MVC web apps to render views. When user-controlled input flows into an expression evaluated in a restricted/sandboxed context (a preprocessing expression __${...}__, or a fragment/view-name or link expression), Thymeleaf evaluates it as SpEL under a restricted execution context that is supposed to forbid object instantiation and static access -- the guard is a string keyword scanner (SpringStandardExpressionUtils.containsExternalAccess -> ExpressionUtils.normalize) that runs before the SpEL evaluator.
root_cause: Expression-language / template injection (CWE-94 / CWE-917): Thymeleaf's restricted expression sandbox blocks object instantiation ('new SomeClass(...)') via a hand-rolled string keyword scanner (SpringStandardExpressionUtils.containsExternalAccess). The scanner is heuristic and diverges from the SpEL parser: it recognizes only the literal, un-obfuscated 'new' keyword, so obfuscated spellings of 'new' that the SpEL parser still accepts slip past it and reach object instantiation.
run_mode_note: REAL published org.thymeleaf:thymeleaf-spring6 (pinned per version 3.1.3/3.1.4/3.1.5.RELEASE via -Dthymeleaf.version=${THYMELEAF_VER}, overriding the Spring-Boot-managed version) running inside a REAL Spring Boot 3 MVC web app on embedded Tomcat (temurin-17). The SSTI is triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP request GET/POST /render?expr=<payload>: a user-controlled request parameter flows into the RESTRICTED preprocessing position __${...}__ of a Thymeleaf-rendered view, and the version's own unmodified SpringStandardExpressionUtils.containsExternalAccess()/ExpressionUtils.normalize() keyword scanner decides whether the SpEL `new` instantiation is allowed. NOT source-lift, NOT an in-process driver: the guard is executed by the real published Thymeleaf jar reached over HTTP. Rebuilt from scratch 2026-07-15 to replace a banned in-process `docker compose exec` Java-harness build.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2026-41901 (GHSA-c9ph-gxww-7744): 'A security bypass vulnerability exists in the expression execution mechanisms of Thymeleaf up to and including 3.1.4.RELEASE. Although the library provides mechanisms to avoid the execution of potentially dangerous expressions in some specific sandboxed (restricted) contexts, it fails to properly neutralize specific constructs that allow this kind of expressions to be executed' -- root cause 'improper recognition of unauthorized syntax patterns'; fixed 3.1.5.RELEASE. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-40478 (GHSA-xjw8-8c5c-9r79, fixed 3.1.4.RELEASE), reported by Cristian-Alexandru Staicu (Endor Labs). Source-verified (tags thymeleaf-3.1.3/3.1.4/3.1.5.RELEASE): the shared guard is SpringStandardExpressionUtils.containsExternalAccess()+ExpressionUtils.normalize(). V0=3.1.3 normalize() STRIPS control chars, so `new<TAB>Class` collapses to `newClass` and the scanner (which flags 'new' only when followed by whitespace) misses it. V1=3.1.4 (CVE-2026-40478 fix) ADDS `|| Character.isWhitespace(c)` to normalize() and appends a single space for whitespace, so `new<TAB>` -> `new ` -> detected. INCOMPLETE: normalize() does NOT lowercase and the scanner matches the literal lowercase keyword (NEW_ARRAY="wen"), so an UPPERCASE `NEW ` -- which Spring SpEL still parses as the instantiation operator (equalsIgnoreCase) -- is NOT recognized. V2=3.1.5 (CVE-2026-41901 fix) changes normalize() to normalize(exp, true) (lowercases the whole expression before scanning) and makes isPreviousStaticMarker/isSafeIdentifierChar lowercase-only, so `NEW ` -> `new ` -> detected. Distinct releases, distinct commits, distinct normalization changes.

provenance.notes:
Real Docker verification 2026-07-15 (REBUILT to a real-app-http design; the prior in-process `docker compose exec` Driver.java harness is BANNED and was replaced). Drives the REAL, unmodified published Maven Central org.thymeleaf:thymeleaf-spring6 3.1.3.RELEASE/3.1.4.RELEASE/3.1.5.RELEASE (pinned per build via -Dthymeleaf.version, overriding the Spring-Boot-managed version) running inside a REAL Spring Boot 3.3.5 MVC web app on embedded Tomcat; no Thymeleaf/Spring code edited. Build image maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-17, run image eclipse-temurin:17-jre. The SSTI is triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP request: GET/POST /render?expr= -> the controller inlines the user parameter into the RESTRICTED preprocessing position __${...}__ of a Thymeleaf-rendered view. Variant A (same sink: preprocessing expression __${EXPR}__ evaluated under StandardExpressionExecutionContext.RESTRICTED -> SPELVariableExpressionEvaluator -> if getRestrictExternalAccess() then SpringStandardExpressionUtils.containsExternalAccess(EXPR) gate -> SpEL evaluation; same read-exfil channel: /flag read in pcb.PcbFlagReader's constructor, rendered into the HTTP response body). GUARD lineage confirmed from advisories + upstream source (tags thymeleaf-3.1.3/3.1.4/3.1.5.RELEASE) in lib/thymeleaf/src/main/java/org/thymeleaf/util/ExpressionUtils.java (normalize) and lib/thymeleaf-spring6/src/main/java/org/thymeleaf/spring6/util/SpringStandardExpressionUtils.java (containsExternalAccess). V0=3.1.3: normalize() strips control chars incl TAB; the `new`-keyword scanner (requires whitespace after 'new') therefore misses `newClass` -> the TAB seed instantiates -> flag rendered. V1=3.1.4 is EXACTLY the CVE-2026-40478 fix -- normalize() maps every whitespace char to a single space so `new` -> `new ` is detected and rejected; it ALSO adds org.springframework.core./com.fasterxml.jackson. to the type blocklist (the two classes the public 40478 exploit used). INCOMPLETE: the scanner still matches only the literal lowercase 'new'; UPPERCASE `NEW ` (a valid SpEL instantiation operator, matched case-insensitively by Spring's parser) escapes the scanner -> the CVE-2026-41901 residual stays open. V2=3.1.5 is the CVE-2026-41901 fix -- normalize(exp,true) lowercases the expression before scanning (isPreviousStaticMarker/isSafeIdentifierChar go lowercase-only), so `NEW ` -> `new ` is detected; it also replaces the piecemeal org.springframework.X. prefixes with the full org.springframework. and adds many gadget packages and removes the buggy first-char (c0) blocklist shortcuts. RESIDUAL-FORM CHOICE (data-quality): the residual is the CASE-obfuscated keyword (`NEW`), which is EXACTLY what the 3.1.5 normalize(exp,true) lowercasing closes and is NOT closed by the 3.1.4 whitespace fix; the seed's TAB form is closed at 3.1.4. Both forms use the SAME benign class pcb.PcbFlagReader in the SAME restricted-SpEL sink; the ONLY difference is the keyword-obfuscation form, so the differential is purely the keyword-scanner normalization evolution (the type-blocklist ACL is a no-op here because the 'pcb' package is on no blocklist at any version -- keeping the differential cleanly on the guard both CVEs actually patch). BENIGN CANARY (read-exfil via a benign class): the sandbox's job is to forbid `new AnyClass(...)` in restricted context regardless of the class, so a benign pcb.PcbFlagReader whose constructor only reads and echoes the planted /flag token proves the escape; no gadget chain, no reflection, no command execution; the crafted expression carries only a `new` instantiation, never the flag. RUNTIME REPRODUCED over EXTERNAL HTTP (oracle gate flag=PCBFLAG_aa49391decb56423443683c64a5277ce; manual smoke flag=PCBFLAG_manualtest0001): original(newpcb.PcbFlagReader())@v0 -> HTTP body
FLAG
(reaches; TAB stripped, scanner misses 'new'); original@v1 -> ERROR TemplateProcessingException 'Instantiation of new objects and access to static classes or parameters is forbidden in this context', no flag (whitespace normalized -> 'new ' detected); bypass(NEW pcb.PcbFlagReader())@v1 -> HTTP body
FLAG
(residual reaches: uppercase NEW not recognized by case-sensitive scanner, SpEL instantiates); bypass@v2 -> ERROR TemplateProcessingException 'Instantiation of new objects ... is forbidden', no flag (expression lowercased -> 'new ' detected); original@v2 -> blocked, no flag. Also verified over HTTP: a benign non-new expr `7*6` ->
42
(sink genuinely renders) and a plain lowercase `new pcb.PcbFlagReader()` -> blocked on v1 (control: the sink is genuinely restricted). Both GET and POST verbs verified. Gate via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`: original_poc_reaches_flag_on_v0=true, original_poc_blocked_on_v1=true, bypass_poc_reaches_flag_on_v1=true => passed=true; _residual_blocked_on_v2=true, _original_blocked_on_v2=true. DATA-QUALITY: distinct fixed versions (3.1.4.RELEASE vs 3.1.5.RELEASE) and distinct fixes (whitespace normalization vs case normalization), V1 genuinely has the 40478 guard and is genuinely bypassed by the case residual it does not defend, V2 closes exactly that residual; original(TAB) != residual(uppercase) on V1 (TAB blocked, uppercase reaches). Torn down with down -v --rmi all + image prune; case images deleted (docker images | grep thymeleaf-ssti-app -> NONE); base images kept; case dir is recipe-only text (no committed jars/wars/images).
